decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: P1 establishes a 21% reduction specifically in training time per epoch; omitting “per epoch” broadens the reported scope.

decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: P1 contains no long-tail result, but an excerpt’s silence does not establish that the entire paper reports none; the Methods summary also attributes long-tail gains to prior work.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1 gives an 18.1% relative gain, while the Methods summary identifies roughly 20% long-tail gains as the prior-work benchmark; describing these magnitudes as consistent is calibrated.

decisions.label: UNSUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: Although T1 supports the approximately 18% gain, P1 does not report the roughly 20% long-tail gain specifically attributed to Sorensen-Nakata et al.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: The 0.006 absolute increase from 0.085 to 0.091 is reasonably and cautiously characterized as modest.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED

numbers.quote: widely credited with roughly 20% relative gains in long-tail Recall@20

decisions.rationale: The numerical phrase refers to the roughly 20% benchmark stated in the Methods summary, even though the claim correctly says P1 itself does not report that gain.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1 supplies the observed gain, but P1 supplies no prior long-tail Recall@20 estimate for a direct evidence-based comparison.
